summary:
Afyonkarahisar has no distinct legal or policing regime on LGBTI+ matters. The province stands entirely under Turkey's national framework, and the draft omnibus justice package reported by Human Rights Watch on 29 October 2025 contains no Afyonkarahisar-specific provision. A visitor in the province is subject to the same national statutes, the same identity-document requirements at checkpoints and the same street-level policing practice documented elsewhere in Turkey.

Human Rights Watch's 29 October 2025 report describes a leaked draft of Türkiye's 11th Judicial Package as one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades. Conduct deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality, including its so-called promotion, would carry up to three years in prison. Participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies would carry up to four years; since same-sex marriage is not legal in Turkey, such ceremonies are by definition symbolic. Gender-affirming care would be restricted, with the surgery age raised from 18 to 25 and permanent infertility made mandatory. Medical professionals would face fines or up to seven years, and transgender patients up to three years for care outside the new limits, a set of penalties that would push treatment into underground settings. Whether the package has since passed is unresolved in the sources.

Kaos GL's 2025 report, A Major Siege against LGBTI+ People in 2025: Hostility Turned into State Policy, documents six right-to-life violations over the year, three recorded as hate-motivated killings, with trans people the most affected. The counts come from media and civil-society reports because the state keeps no official hate-crime statistics. The report also records 89 torture or ill-treatment violations, up from 51, mostly linked to peaceful assembly, together with 336 assembly violations and 313 liberty violations. The roughly 2.5-fold rise in liberty violations consists mostly of detentions, alongside event-specific bans and violent police attacks on peaceful gatherings. It describes hostility institutionalised under Year of the Family instructions to public institutions, hate speech from senior officials, censored broadcasts and cancelled artistic events as national practice. The report contains no Afyonkarahisar-specific finding; it describes the country-wide framework that governs the province.
tangentialFactors:
The national pattern documented in the Kaos GL report is drawn from media and civil-society monitoring rather than official statistics, since Turkey maintains no hate-crime data series. Raw counts of violations therefore track both reporting capacity and population distribution across provinces, and their concentration in large cities such as Istanbul and Ankara does not by itself establish that smaller provinces are safer.

The draft 11th Judicial Package was still unenacted when Human Rights Watch reported on it in October 2025, and the sources do not resolve whether it has since been adopted. A visitor should treat the existing national statutes and policing practice as the operative baseline, with the draft as an unresolved downside risk.
localsOnly:
Residents of Afyonkarahisar live under the same national framework as visitors, with no province-specific legal protections or policing directives on LGBTI+ matters. Kaos GL's documentation of assembly and liberty violations, and of hostility institutionalised through Year of the Family instructions to public institutions, applies to residents organising or attending events in the province.

Gender-affirming care restrictions in the draft judicial package, including the raised surgery age and mandatory infertility requirement, would fall on residents seeking treatment within Turkey's healthcare system rather than on short-term visitors paying privately. Medical professionals in the province would face the fines and prison terms described in the draft if it is enacted.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted since the October 2025 Human Rights Watch report is unresolved in the sources.

No Afyonkarahisar-specific incident, enforcement action, or local official statement on LGBTI+ matters appears in the inventory; the province-level picture is inferred from the absence of any such finding rather than from affirmative local reporting.

The Kaos GL violation counts are compiled from media and civil-society reports, not official state data, and the sources provide no per-capita or provincial breakdown.
